_comment: P-306 / D-262 condition 1: the containers signature policy the workspace-host bootc
image MUST ship at /etc/containers/policy.json.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The centos-bootc base ships a policy whose default is
{"type": "insecureAcceptAnything"} — measured, and reproduced as PROBE C in
p306-signature-policy-probe.sh, which copies an UNSIGNED image with exit 0. So adopting
bootc gives the verification MECHANISM, defaulted OFF. If P-306 removes the tarball's
minisign check because "bootc verifies now" and nobody ships this file, the customer host
verifies NOTHING and is strictly weaker than the path it replaced.
SUBSTITUTION POINTS — this is a TEMPLATE, not a finished policy. Two values are
deliberately placeholders because the artifacts that define them do not exist yet:
<RELEASE_REGISTRY_NAMESPACE>  the registry repo the release is published to. The current
release path is an HTTPS TARBALL, not a registry, so this
namespace is P-307's to establish.
/etc/pki/papercusp/release-signing.pub  the sigstore PUBLIC key. P-308's `cosign sign`
produces the matching signature; the key is baked into the
image at build time, never fetched at run time.
Leaving a placeholder in place makes the policy fail CLOSED (the reference cannot match),
which is the correct direction for an unfinished supply chain.
COUPLING (D-262 condition 3): this policy and P-308's signing are ONE unit. Shipping this
without the signature bricks upgrades; shipping the signature without this verifies nothing.
The `default: reject` below is load-bearing. Do NOT soften it to insecureAcceptAnything to
make an unrelated pull work — add a narrow transport entry for that specific source instead.
